answer: Behavioral trail clustering. The mechanism groups agent identities by overlap in transaction timing, counterparties, and infrastructure fingerprints, then scores each cluster against a baseline of independent actors. A cluster whose internal correlation reaches its zenith while its external links stay thin is flagged, and every identity in it is throttled or frozen. Identity records live in a cold vault with signed timestamps, so retroactive edits are detectable. Detection runs on shale-like layering: weak signals from many sessions accumulate until the cluster crosses threshold.
